html:
SMTO-EXE-0241 — The Docker action was stopped before it finished

GUID: f2e6a5c7-d2d4-5718-8ee7-443cd334a939
Slug: docker-operation-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker action was cancelled while it was running. If it had already started, some of its changes may have happened, for example a container may have started or an image may be partly downloaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to show the current state of the containers, images or Compose project that the action was working on. Listing what is there doesn't change anything and shows how far the stopped action got.
  2. Compare that with what you wanted and note what is still missing. Repeating the whole action could start or change things a second time.
  3. Ask SMTO to do only the remaining part, and approve the new request if SMTO asks. A new, smaller request finishes the job without redoing what already happened.

What success looks like

  • The containers, images or project now look the way you wanted, and SMTO reports success for the new request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the full action until you've checked what the stopped one already did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Docker operation on the selected Gateway observed cancellation at a checkpoint; if it had already started changing Engine or registry state, the receipt keeps those effects as unknown rather than claiming nothing ran.

What this means

  • The operation checkpoint observed cancellation, retaining whether a mutation had already started. Post-dispatch service handling preserves unknown effects rather than claiming the operation never ran. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The operation checkpoint observed cancellation, retaining whether a mutation had already started. Post-dispatch service handling preserves unknown effects rather than claiming the operation never ran.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect mutation/effect flags, object identity and known_completed steps before planning further work.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cancellation receipt (known_completed, object_id, reconciliation fields) and the current Engine or registry state with read-only tools (docker.containers, docker.images, docker.compose_ps). Issue a new, separately approved request only for the work that is still needed.
  • Inspect the original cancellation receipt and Engine/registry state; issue new work only for what remains necessary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Original Docker effects and owned transport/process cleanup are settled before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
